newsitem.title: GERMANY: Fresenius Medical plans dividend from 1997.
newsitem.headline: Fresenius Medical plans dividend from 1997.

text.p: German medical technology group Fresenius Medical Care said on Tuesday it planned to start paying dividends on its ordinary and preferred shares as of 1997.
Chairman Gerd Krick told a news conference the move would be in Fresenius Medical's own interests and in those of its parent Fresenius AG.

Krick, also chairman of Fresenius, said Fresenius Medical Care's debts would be scaled back through "internal growth" but that the unit would also keep open the chance of using a capital increase to finance further growth in the future.
The Fresenius group had "barely achieved" its goal of raising sales by a double digit rate in the first quarter, Krick said.
He declined to give further details.
Fresenius Medical Care is the world's largest dialysis company and is listed on the New York bourse.
The company was formed in October 1996 when Fresenius merged its core dialysis business with National Medical Care, which it acquired from U.S. group W.R. Grace last year.
